Using the standard ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule on TypeScript or Svelte files containing TypeScript causes false positives on type annotations (such as type imports, interface definitions, and type-annotation parameter names). This is why parameter names in function type signatures had to be prefixed with `_` across multiple component files (e.g., `_base64`, `_mimeType`, `_wig`, `_actionId`, etc.).

To resolve this cleanly and avoid polluting your type definitions with underscores, you should disable the base `no-unused-vars` rule for TypeScript/Svelte files and either:
1. Rely on the TypeScript compiler / `svelte-check` (via `"noUnusedLocals": true` and `"noUnusedParameters": true` in `tsconfig.json`), which natively and accurately handles unused variables/parameters without false positives.
2. Use the `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` rule from `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` which is designed to understand TypeScript syntax.

`globals.browser` and `globals.node` are being applied together to every file. This can mask real `no-undef` issues (e.g., accidentally using `navigator`/`window` in server-only code like `src/routes/api/**` or pipelines) because both environments’ globals are always considered defined. Prefer scoping browser globals to UI/client code and node globals to server/pipeline code so ESLint still catches cross-environment mistakes.

If `FileReader.result` is not a string (or if the read fails), the handler currently returns silently. That can leave a stale preview and gives the user no feedback that the upload failed. Consider setting an error message (and optionally clearing `previewUrl`) and wiring `reader.onerror` so failures are visible.
